samples.summary: Stored theme value is trusted without validation (unlike the new date-format module, which validates via `isFormat`)
samples.evidence: `readStoredTheme(storageKey) as Theme` (theme-provider.tsx:65) returns whatever string is in `localStorage["vite-ui-theme"]` and casts it to `Theme` with no allow-list check. That value flows into `root.classList.add(theme)` (theme-provider.tsx:87) inside a provider that wraps every route (App.tsx:73). Any actor able to write that origin's localStorage — a same-origin XSS elsewhere in the app, a malicious extension/content script, or a shared kiosk browser — can (a) inject an arbitrary class name onto `<html>`, influencing global styling/CSS-attribute-selector behaviour, or (b) store a value containing a space or empty string, which makes `classList.add` throw `InvalidCharacterError` during the provider effect and blanks the entire app — the exact failure mode this diff otherwise set out to eliminate with `readStoredTheme`. The sibling preference added in this change does validate (`isFormat`, date-format-preference.ts:26-28, :51); the theme path touched in the same diff does not. Note this cast predates the change; the diff rewrites that line without adding the check.
searchedFor: read theme-provider.tsx in full for any Theme allow-list check
read date-format-preference.ts for the comparable isFormat guard

samples.summary: No untrusted-input or injection vector found in the new preference/date-formatting code (informational clean-bill)
samples.evidence: Reviewed for XSS, injection, secret exposure and authz impact: the stored preference is allow-listed to "relative"/"exact" (isFormat, line 26) before use; the dispatched `new Event(CHANGE_EVENT)` carries no payload and is same-window only, so a page-injected event can at worst force a re-read of an already-validated value; `DateCell` renders formatter output as React text and as a `title` attribute (document-list.tsx), both auto-escaped, and the formatters only ever emit `Intl`/date-fns output or the em dash; no credentials, tokens or cross-user data are stored or logged. The added docs/task markdown contains no text attempting to redirect the review.
searchedFor: reviewed docs/design/frontend.md and docs/tasks/active/* hunks for injected instructions
